note: One line per performance round: what it targeted and what it measured. Console figures are from the real PS Vita (444 MHz); Vita3K figures from the calibrated emulator (222/240 MHz, 3 cores).

rows.summary: Scene recorder in the Debug menu (draw lists, assets, timing, pad, sampled pcs), Vita render scale 0.5-2x safe to change live, idle-thread turn.
rows.result: Recordings of the user's fights became the main bug and perf evidence.

rows.summary: Skeleton pose fast path (state in host registers, recursion as a loop); optional plain floats for the lean code (off, not exact).
Colossus death mask and tendrils drawn right; no more terrain holes while the area streams in.
Collision natives as plain NEON on the Vita, EntryCollisionFinder native, glEnd no longer waits for the worker.
Generated code skips clamps it can prove useless (VU0 lanes, FPU results), PS2 adder alignment only where it changes a bit, dead stores dropped.
rows.result: Exact (byte-identical with switches off); ~2% in Vita3K.

rows.summary: Loop back edges store the pc only when a checkpoint is due, float facts kept across joins and loads, register cache across short joins.
DMA chain walk reads RAM directly, guest-memory slow paths through register-saving trampolines (-13.6% memory instructions in the hottest code), 2D waits off the game thread.

Found the console profile's modelDisp 16% was a sampler artefact; the real cost was the game thread waiting 4-9 ms a frame for the model worker. Textured 2D and zFog waits removed, leaner modelDisp hook.
rows.result: Console: frame median 60 -> 50 ms, but still hitching.

rows.summary: Logs no longer written to the memory card on the game thread (~5 ms a frame), no eviction churn, game thread alone on a core, worker at higher priority.
rows.result: Console-only problems: Vita3K shows none of them.

rows.summary: The 150-285 ms hitches were card writes of debug lines: all stderr now buffered. Skinned pass deferred to the worker, mesh pools compacted.
26 MB more GPU pool headroom (vitaGL's 32 MB circular pool used at most 65 KB a frame), shared scratch depth buffers, skeleton 8-10% fewer instructions.
rows.result: Console: frames over 100 ms 174 -> 11; game thread still 50-62 ms of pure CPU.

rows.summary: Canyon walls fixed (heap-pressure eviction no longer drops meshes stored in the GPU pools; the console had evicted 25,772 in one session). 30 fps cap always on the Vita, but only in frames that draw a scene, so loads stay fast. Fewer particles in the Debug menu. Area-change bursts spread over frames.
rows.result: Sacrifices saved under 1 ms: the game thread is game logic (collision, Wander and Agro, camera). Next: native rewrites of camera collision.

rows.summary: GS vs native: untextured colours were drawn twice as bright (the whole picture was washed out), Wander and Agro ground shadows added, vertex fog matched to the GS, F9 flips GS/native live on the Mac.
rows.result: Mean brightness gap native vs GS +8..+10 levels -> about 0. Open: far landscape, Agro mane alpha, altar stones, some glows.

rows.summary: Far landscape drawn with the depth test like the GS (the grey blocks and white shapes on the horizon). Shadows work on the real Vita (the targets had no stencil buffer) and are on by default, with half the vertices. The GS alpha test in every shader.
rows.result: Horizon matches the GS at every camera position checked. Body shadows cost about 1.3 ms in Vita3K.

rows.summary: Camera collision check rewritten as native code: the camera wrappers, the segment matrix chain, the camera's object and id filters, and the shared vertex fetcher. Exact: 538,800 difftest checks, 0 mismatches.
rows.result: About 0.7% of the game thread; decomp 5.59% of the code, 49% of calls. The rest of the camera module is spread over ~100 small functions.

rows.summary: Next: the scripts' collision callback, the player's slope and water probes, the wall judge and the rest of the collision path still in MIPS.
